scope: Proposition G.1 (Cube comparison) of the manuscript “Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions” (preprints/Quasipolynomial-Bounds-for-Arithmetic-Progressions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 159 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 481eaf7730dc4d58), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 147. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Use the coefficient law of Section F, with the numbers of dedicated product blocks and kernel columns chosen sufficiently large as polynomials of the initial dimensions for the fixed cube-order and derivative ranges. Assume the hypotheses of Lemma F.7. Fix a pre-cost parameter slice B, a bounded cube order q, and a pre accuracy ε > 0. The averaged sampled-cube functional (Pω)ω 7−→ EψEt∈Cubq(B) Y ω Pω(ψ(tω)) is, uniformly for arbitrary |Pω| ≤ 1, within ε of a mixture of ambient cube functionals X α cαEu∈Cubq(U) Y ω Pω(uω)Jα,ω(uω). The Jα,ω are allowed site twists of pre complexity, and P α |cα| is pre-bounded. Mixtures can be replaced by finite sums to any prescribed accuracy. The bounds do not use σ, L, R, or the heights of the subspaces Wh.
